headline: What Is the
Yield Curve,
and Why Does
It Get Watched?
slides.subtitle:
A 60-second explainer on a famous
bond market chart.

slides.title: In One Sentence
slides.big: The yield curve plots what the US government pays to borrow for different lengths of time.
slides.body: Short-term to long-term Treasuries, from 1 month to 30 years, lined up on one chart.

slides.title: How It Works
items: Normal: longer loans pay higher yields.
Flat: short and long yields are close.
slides.footer: Yields reflect rate expectations and risk.
slides.disclaimer: For informational purposes only. Not investment advice.

slides.title: Why It Matters to You
slides.big: It reflects what markets expect for rates, growth and inflation.
slides.body: Long-term yields influence mortgage rates. An inverted curve has often come before past recessions, but it is not a guarantee.
slides.source: Source: Federal Reserve research, US Treasury

slides.title: Remember This
items: It compares Treasury yields by maturity.
